questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, I prioritised an English-speaking university. I have previously been in Canada and thought it would be interesting to both study there but also travel around.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They send different informative emails and I think those were useful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As exchange students at the science faculty, we were assigned an advisor who held an information meeting a couple of days before classes started. She explained some of the things we should be aware of when choosing or changing courses and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We used Facebook groups to search for apartments and were lucky to find it fast. But there seemed to be a lot of scammers in those groups so it took a while to scan through those. At McGill there are not a lot of on campus housing for exchange students and the housing are in general mostly for first year students. That is something to have in mind. It was also a lot cheaper to live off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not allowed for the landlords in Montreals to obtain a deposit beforehand. The Plateau area is nice to live in for students - it has a Nørrebro-vibe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to obtain and upload some different documents from KU to minerva, which is their version of Kunet. A English proficiency letter, a scan of passport, transcript that were signed and nomination letter.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I just used the instructions from the application sheet from kunet which I found to be enough.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the classes I wanted to take overlapped so I would say that I got 3/4 of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You get a time slot for course registration and you have to enrol at that time. Thereafter it is easy to change courses and this can be done up until two weeks after the classes begin. So if you didn't get a class it is a good idea to check Minerva regularly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was similar to courses at KU. You just need to have four courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The main difference is that there are quizzes, midterms, presentations and assignments during the semester (in some courses) that is a part of the final grade. I had four really different courses with different styles of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHAR300 - Drug Action 
PHGY488 - Stem Cel Biology 
COMP204 - Programming for Life Science 
WCOM314 - Communicating Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think WCOM314 was really a great course because it was really different from what I'm used to at university and it gave some tools and made me reflect on how to write and talk about science to different audiences.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not so much. I had to buy a duvet and some smaller things for the kitchen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices was kind of similar with things in Copenhagen. Off campus housing were cheaper than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In the beginning they have intro which is called frosh. I attended the outdoor-frosh which was a four day trip to a campsite and about half of us were exchange students. This was a great way to meet other students and also go on a trip in the nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car (google "car rental McGill" to get a link through McGill for student discount) and go the many national parks in Quebec.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend frosh in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They speak French in Montreal and I don't. It is good to know some basics especially when going other places in Quebec.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It feels like a lot of work during the semester with assignments and such, but because they count in the final grade, there is less pressure on the exams.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend social activities and try to go to some of the club meetings.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To study and live in another country is very interesting and also challenging to balance going out on trips in the weekends and also doing school. But I found it very rewarding to give myself time to relax and not to do school work in most of my weekends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing assignments weekly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
